# Build and test only

These are used only to compile, type-check, bundle and test the code, or to rebuild bundled map tiles. Nothing from them ships in the product; only what they produce does.

## npm:@digitalbazaar/eddsa-jcs-2022-cryptosuite

**What it provides.** The reference eddsa-jcs-2022 cryptosuite, used only in tests to check our own credential proofs.

**Why it is needed.** Checks in tests that credentials we sign verify with the reference implementation and that its proofs verify with ours, and gives the RFC 8785 canonical form our canonical JSON is compared with. Nothing from it ships. Without it we would trust our own reading of the specification alone.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | npm package |
| Pinned version or digest | `1.0.0` |
| Architecture component | `extension` |
| Used in | `package.json` |
| Scope | Test only: not shipped |
| Licence | BSD-3-Clause |
| Cryptography | None |
| Air gap | Works with no internet access |
| Compliance fit | Pass with conditions |
| Controls | SA-11, SA-15, SR-3 |
| Security fixes | Exact pin in the root lockfile; advisories are recorded by the daily full npm audit (compliance-scheduled.yml, report-only); the blocking CI audit omits devDependencies. No Dependabot: bumped by hand in a reviewed PR. |
| Reviewed | Claude (agent review); owner approved 2026-11-24 ("approved", 71-01 package check), 2026-11-24 |

Conditions:

- Test only: a devDependency used as an oracle in src/test; no file outside src/test may import it, and it never ships (node\_modules, src and dist/test are excluded from the extension package; the hub, relay and workbench images build from their own lockfiles).
- No build provenance: the npm registry signature is checked (all 25 packages of the tree valid on 2026-11-24, 71-01-PACKAGE-CHECK.md), but the tarball cannot be tied to a commit by a signature; the GitHub release tag exists for the pinned version.
- Not updated since its only release (1.0.0, 2024-11-08, two years old); it predates the W3C Recommendation of 2025-05-15, so the frozen W3C vectors in our test are the arbiter if the two ever disagree.

## npm:@digitalbazaar/vc

**What it provides.** The reference Verifiable Credentials library, used only in tests to issue and verify credentials against ours.

**Why it is needed.** Issues and verifies credentials in tests with a static document loader that holds the needed contexts and refuses any other address, so no test reaches the network. Nothing from it ships. Without it we would trust our own reading of the specification alone.

## npm:@digitalbazaar/vc-bitstring-status-list

**What it provides.** The reference Bitstring Status List library, used only in tests to check our status lists.

## npm:@jsquash/jpeg

**What it provides.** Encodes JPEG images for the offline globe tiles and environment packs built by scripts/build-globe-tiles.mjs and scripts/generate-env-pack.mjs.

**Why it is needed.** Decodes the source world image when a developer rebuilds the COP map's bundled globe tiles (scripts/build-globe-tiles.mjs). Without it the tile builder would need a native image tool on the developer's machine. Nothing from it ships; only the tiles it helps make.

## npm:@jsquash/webp

**What it provides.** Encodes WebP images for the offline globe tiles and environment packs (scripts/lib/webp.mjs).

**Why it is needed.** Encodes the WebP map tiles that ship with the COP map: the bundled globe tiles and the environment pack tiles (scripts/lib/webp.mjs). These tiles let the map work offline. Without it the tiles would need a native encoder on the build machine. It runs only when a developer rebuilds tiles; the encoder never ships.

## npm:@types/node

**What it provides.** Type definitions for Node.js, used by the TypeScript type check of the extension, relay, hub, compliance package and workbench.

**Why it is needed.** Lets the TypeScript type check understand the Node.js APIs used by the extension, relay, hub, compliance package and workbench. Without it the type check fails on every Node.js import, and type errors would only show up when the code runs. Types only: nothing ships. *This role is waiting for the owner to confirm it.*

## npm:@vscode/test-electron

**What it provides.** Downloads a VS Code build and runs the end-to-end tests in it.

**Why it is needed.** Downloads a real VS Code build and runs the end-to-end tests inside it (the e2e CI job). Without it the extension could only be tested outside the editor, and faults in how it works with the editor would first appear for users.

## npm:esbuild

**What it provides.** Bundles the relay, the hub, the workbench engine bundle and test build (workbench/tools/build-engine.mjs, workbench/scripts/build.mjs), and the vendored libraries (pptxgenjs, the MCP client, Yjs) in scripts/vendor-libs.mjs.

**Why it is needed.** Bundles the relay and hub into single files for their images, the engine code the workbench backend reuses (the team parser) and the workbench test build, and pptxgenjs, the MCP client and Yjs into the extension's vendor/ folder. Bundling lets the extension and the images ship without extra node\_modules, which keeps the shipped files few and reviewable. *This role is waiting for the owner to confirm it.*
